scope: Independent static review of isolated frontend batch wiring; no execution, promotion or performance claim.
verdict: No source-level correctness blocker found in this snapshot. Coherent frontend compilation/tests remain separate.
reviewed_contracts: Optional default None leaves original reduce_sum path available. Only independent components of one weighted sum are chunked; active pending visitation/discovery order remain unchanged.
Input validation includes zero-weight labels and stops at first invalid input; earlier native/output failure takes precedence over saved later validation failure.
Native/codec/conversion errors stay ordered per-item errors. Later errors are counted but later conditions/results never enter the consumed logical prefix.

Whole-batch executed native work is recorded before logical commits; unknown work inside native Err stays explicitly incomplete. Logical/memoized prefix counts remain separate from actual/speculative counters.
Per-item ordered memo snapshots preserve consumed-prefix peak accounting for the actual execution. Retained-byte caps remain native owned-payload caps, not decoded/CAS scratch bounds.
Returned terms/residuals are validated under the unchanged admitted-domain contract; only NoApplicableRule residuals may cancel within the weighted sum. Other failures remain explicit.
Final source replay and target/every-basis-derivative reconstruction callsites remain in place. No lower-level pending queue or scalar algebra is replaced.
qualifications: Extra cancellation polls can stop after native work before committing a finished batch; tests explicitly account that work and retain no later guards. This is an opt-in bounded-batch cancellation contract.

Symbolica global registry export prevents a universal identical cache-byte/hit/peak claim when external registrations or interleaved frontend CAS change global state. Controlled native serial/batch tests establish their own scoped equality only.
Private result-shape invariants (ordered item/snapshot/window counts) are supplied by the native API and its tests. The wrapper does not ingest an untrusted serialized batch.
